subject: general
question: Who described Mahatma Gandhi as "the great soul in beggar's garb"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabindranath Tagore.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **In April 1893**, Gandhi sailed for South Africa, a young and inexperienced barrister in search of fortune.
 
• **In January 1915** he finally returned to India with no possessions and with only one ambition - to serve his people. 
 
• Rabindranath Tagore described Mahatma Gandhi as** "the great soul in beggar's garb".**
 
• At the end of his year's wanderings, Gandhi settled down on the bank of the river Sabarmati, on the outskirts of Ahmedabad.
 
• He founded an ashram in **May 1915.**
 
• He called it the **Satyagraha Ashram.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rabindranath Tagore was the youngest son of Debendranath Tagore.
 
• He was the** leader of the Brahmo Samaj.**
 
• He was educated at home; and although at seventeen he was sent to England for formal schooling.
 
• He was knighted by the ruling British Government in **1915**.
 
• Within a few years he resigned the honor as a protest against British policies in India.
